history.summary: South Indian-style shrine of Goddess Bhuvaneshwari (a Mahavidya form of Parvati, 'queen of the universe') on a 350-ft hilltop in Telco Colony (Tata Motors colony), Kharangajhar, Jamshedpur. Construction was completed in 1978 by Swami Ranga Rajan (a Tamil priest; some sources spell Rangarajan). The 2-acre complex has Dravidian architecture with a 64-ft five-tiered rajagopuram topped by five kalasams and a 36-ft garbhagriha; its eight pillars are believed to house eight incarnations of the goddess. An adjoining Krishna temple was established by the local Kerala community. It is managed by a trust and draws 5,000-10,000 visitors during Navratri. CSV town 'Jamshedpur' is coarse - corrected to Telco, Jamshedpur.

name: Bhuvaneshwari Temple
town_description: Jamshedpur, known as the Steel City of India, is the largest city in Jharkhand. Founded by Jamsetji Tata as a planned industrial town around Tata Steel (TISCO), the settlement was called Sakchi until it was renamed Jamshedpur in 1919. The city sits at the confluence of the Kharkai and Subarnarekha rivers in East Singhbhum district, and its neighbourhoods (Telco, Golmuri, Sakchi, Kadma, Parsudih, Sidhgora) grew around Tata Steel and its subsidiary companies.

travel.road: Driveable road up the hill within Telco Colony; city buses and autos connect from Jamshedpur town

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (winter); Navratri is the major festival period
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hours not published by a reliable source; some travel sites say the temple is open to visitors throughout the day (verify)
